Urban heat islands—metropolitan zones that register markedly higher ambient temperatures than
surrounding rural landscapes—exemplify how anthropogenic land-use alterations reshape local
microclimates. Impervious asphalt roads, concrete high-rises, and dark-coloured rooftops absorb
prodigious quantities of solar radiation during the day and re-emit that thermal energy slowly
throughout the night, preventing nocturnal cooling. Compounded by waste heat from vehicular
exhaust and air-conditioning units, this phenomenon exacerbates heat-related morbidity, escalates
peak electricity demand, and degrades urban air quality. Mitigating urban heat islands requires an
integrated spatial strategy: expanding urban tree canopies, mandating high-albedo "cool roofs,"
and restoring permeable blue-green corridors that promote evaporative cooling and stormwater
retention.

Excessive rainfall in cities traps warm air beneath dense cloud cover.

Comprehension Passage – II (Questions 46 – 50): Read the following passage carefully and
answer the questions that follow.
The decipherment of ancient scripts has repeatedly transformed historiography from speculative
conjecture into documented chronology. Before Jean-François Champollion unlocked the phonetic
and ideographic duality of Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822 using the trilingual Rosetta Stone, millennia
of Pharaonic annals remained mute. Similarly, James Prinsep's painstaking epigraphic decoding of
the Brahmi script in the 1830s resurrected the forgotten edicts of Emperor Ashoka, illuminating the
administrative ethics and dhamma diplomacy of Mauryan India. Yet, several enigmatic writing
systems—most notably the Indus Valley script and Linear A of Minoan Crete—continue to resist
consensus decipherment due to the brevity of surviving inscriptions and the absence of bilingual
texts.

options: He translated the Rosetta Stone into classical Sanskrit.
He decoded the Brahmi script, revealing Emperor Ashoka's edicts and Mauryan administrative ethics.
He deciphered the Indus Valley seals found at Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
He proved that Linear A of Minoan Crete was derived from Vedic Sanskrit.
